monoclonal antibodies can be produced against two structually related cytokines, TNF-alpha and beta, that can be used to purify these cytokines and to develop specific immunoassay techniques for their detection.

monoclonal antibodies to TNF-alpha and beta were produced and used for the purification of the recombinant proteins from E. coli, the development of immunoassays for the detection of these cytokines, and for defining antigenic and functional regions of the proteins.

the development of monoclonal antibodies to TNFs that are useful in a variety of applications, including the purification of recombinant cytokines, development of immunoassays to measure TNFs, and as probes to study the structure and functional domains of the cytokines.

monoclonal antibodies can be utilized as specific immunoadsorbants to purify TNF-alpha and/or TNF-beta from crude cell extracts, as well as for specific immunoassay development, and that the use of these antibodies as probes has defined the structural and functional domains of both TNF-alpha as well as TNF-beta.

the monoclonal antibody approach has been successfully utilized to produce reagents which have been useful for the purification of both TNF-alpha, TNF-beta and their related proteins.

monoclonal antibodies are useful tools for defining antigenic domains of cytokines and for the purification of these molecules from biological sources.
